Resealed 2026-09-29 by `W47-FIX` under the integrator's dispatch in docs/program/dispatch/W47-FIX-DISPATCH.md section 4, repairing F1 (docs/program/reviews/W47-JUDGE-X.md section 3) as `W47-JUDGE-Y` narrowed it (section 15.2). ONE DESCRIPTION MOVES AND NOTHING ELSE: ChangePasswordRequest.new_password.description said "this surface declares no minimum length, no complexity rule, no history and no expiry", and `R-48`'s src/auditmanager/access/policy.py enforces a minimum of 8 and a contextual blocklist on this exact operation -- driven by X against the built API: new_password of 7 characters answers 422 validation_failed, "a password must be at least 8 characters". X argued the word "declares" was defensible for a document whose schema minLength is 1; Y falsified that from the next clause of the same description, which declares a rule in prose ("A value equal to `current_password` is `validation_failed`"), so "declares" already includes prose in this document's own vocabulary. And web/src/features/change-password/ui/change-password-form.tsx carries minLength={8} twice: the only client in this tree already carries a number the contract called undeclared, and did not learn it from the contract. THE CORRECTION DOES NOT RESTATE THE POLICY, and that is the point rather than an economy: writing "minimum 8" into the contract would give the transport document a second authority over policy.py, make every future policy change a reseal, and destroy the property `R-48` was built for -- policy.py argues the policy belongs at the access boundary precisely so a deployment can change it without renegotiating the contract. So the sentence stops claiming there is no policy instead of publishing the policy. Only "no minimum length, no complexity rule" were false; "no history and no expiry" are true of policy.py, which enforces neither, and they stay. The wording is the integrator's, fixed in the dispatch and used verbatim. NO COUNT MOVES: paths / operations / component schemas stay at 17 / 20 / 61, exactly as `W47-LOCK` left them, and the error catalog stays at 22 and stays frozen. No path, operation, schema, property, required list, bound or error code is added, removed or changed, so every D-102/D-105 pin was checked and none of them moves: the surface triple (test_doc_prose_facts.py), FROZEN_OPERATION_COUNT / FROZEN_SCHEMA_COUNT (test_openapi_conformance.py), PATH_COUNT / OPERATION_COUNT / SCHEMA_COUNT (test_served_document_and_health_plane.py) and the error catalog count all already read the values this reseal leaves unchanged. THIS HAD TO BE A RESEAL RATHER THAN AN EDIT for `D-18`'s reason, which `W42-SEAL` states first: the conformance gate drops description as annotation under N4, so a corrected sentence is invisible to it and reaches a reader only through these four documents moving together -- contracts/api/v1/openapi.json, the byte-identical mirror web/openapi/openapi.json, the regenerated client under web/src/shared/api/generated/, and the digest in this file. The sentence lives in no `.md`: `grep -rln "declares no minimum length"` finds the three documents above and the dispatch brief that quotes it, and nothing else, so nothing in prose rides along. content_commit names f6d1fa6 ("repair(W47-FIX): D-101 closed -- the shipped default joins the contextual blocklist"), the nearest commit that made this description's subject true in its final shape -- the policy this operation enforces gained its fourth contextual entry there -- for the reason `W46-SEAL`'s, `W45-BLOCKS`'s and `W42-SEAL`'s notes give: a commit cannot name itself, and this reseal lands all four documents in one commit. UploadDocumentRequest.section and DocumentVersion.section are added, both optional, drawing from the new ProjectSection enum -- legacy's fourteen project sections (D-56). The field lives on document, not document_version or project: it classifies what a document IS, not which revision of its bytes is being read, and a project holds many sections rather than being one -- argued in full in docs/program/W46-SEAL.md section 2. It is optional rather than required because the column starts with no rows to backfill and forcing every caller -- tests/e2e/**, which this stream does not own, among them -- to name a section it may not know would fabricate a classification AGENTS.md section 4 forbids inventing; a document nobody has classified yet is a real state and is never defaulted to one of the fourteen. One operation is added -- getDashboardSummary, GET /dashboard -- under R-44, the integrator's decision against the cheaper path: three of the four dashboard panels (documents per project, findings by verdict, run activity and spend) are already reachable by walking listProjects, listDecisions and listRuns, and the ruling is that the reseal this wave opens anyway should carry one aggregate read serving all four rather than three client-side walks a later aggregate read would only delete -- R-24's own argument, one level up: it was ruled for a listing operation and against a walk, so founding a dashboard on walks over the operation that exists to prevent walks would be an odd inheritance. Resealed 2026-09-25 by W45-BLOCKS. One operation is added -- getVersionBlocks, GET /versions/{version_uid}/blocks -- the first half of R-23's block markup: page_geometry_extraction writes a real bbox per extracted text line (contracts/analysis/v1/stage-registry.json declares this stage's execution.model_routed:false, so D-70's blocked provider key does not gate it) and this operation reads that geometry back. Keyed by version_uid rather than by run_id, because the geometry is a deterministic property of the version and not of any one run of it. An unknown version answers 404 not_found. A version that exists but whose most recently successful run never reached page_geometry_extraction -- or has no run at all -- answers 200 with status:"not_produced" and blocks:[]; a version whose geometry was produced and genuinely has none answers 200 with status:"produced" and blocks:[] -- the same bytes for blocks, different bytes for status, which is the field a caller reads to tell the two apart. It carries no crops: page_geometry_extraction's second artifact, the page-crop manifest, is unconditionally empty in this pipeline (crop_policy:"none") and is a separate artifact this operation does not expose at all, rather than an always-[] field shipped unexplained. Two component schemas were added, VersionBlockIndex and BlockGeometry; BlockGeometry's bbox is inline (an object with x0/y0/x1/y1), not a third schema, so a nested Pydantic model would not mint one FastAPI's generated document and the frozen contract would then disagree about. No error code was added: the only refusal this operation needs, not_found, is already in the twenty-two-code catalog. Paths, operations and component schemas move from 15 / 18 / 51 to 16 / 19 / 53.

Resealed 2026-09-23 by W39-REVOKE under owner ruling R-26 (docs/program/OWNER_RULINGS_2026-09-17.md), which rules four account guards into the alpha. This is the one of the four that CANNOT be added later: the other three make an account weak now and are fixed by adding them, while a credential already issued stays valid until it expires and no later work reaches one already sitting in a browser. One operation is added -- changePassword, POST /auth/password -- and it carries revocation with it, because the two share one mechanism: migration 0007_credential_epoch adds app_user.token_epoch, every minted credential carries the epoch it was minted under, the seam compares the two on every guarded request, and changePassword raises the column in the same UPDATE that writes the new digest. Raising it invalidates every credential ever minted for that account with no denylist kept anywhere. Revocation gets NO operation: taking credentials away from accounts whose passwords nobody is changing is an operator's action (python -m auditmanager.access.revoke) and publishing it would require deciding who may revoke whom, which is the role vocabulary T-6 forbids inventing at this seam. ONE component schema was added, ChangePasswordRequest; NO response schema was, because changePassword answers IssueTokenResponse -- a credential and its lifetime is one shape and the document already had a name for it. No error code was added: a wrong current password is authentication_required and a new password equal to the current one is validation_failed. Paths, operations and component schemas move from 14 / 17 / 50 to 15 / 18 / 51. Every credential minted before this reseal is refused from the moment it lands, because it carries no epoch; everyone signs in again once, which is the intended effect of a change whose purpose is that credentials can be taken away. R-37, closing DEBT_REGISTER.md D-86: DecisionEvent.author_label and DecisionRecord.author_label described themselves as 'one configured local reviewer label ... a label, not a subject identity'. Wave 41 (D-78) made the server write the authenticated reviewer instead of a constant, which made that sentence false, and the owner has now ruled that what it writes is the reviewer's DISPLAY NAME rather than their login -- this is the field another reviewer reads on a decision somebody else took, and a login is an address. The schema does not move: same type, same minLength 1, same maxLength 128, so nothing frozen changed in the sense the freeze means. The sentence was carried TWICE and both copies are corrected; DecisionRecord restates DecisionEvent's properties rather than composing them with allOf, so a reseal that corrected one would have left listDecisions describing the field falsely. An account that has chosen no display name records its login, which is server-held, unique and 1..100 characters -- inside author_label's bounds by construction and not by luck. Migration 0009_reviewer_display_name adds app_user.display_name, nullable so that 'has not chosen a name' stays distinguishable from 'chose their login'.

R-29, closing DEBT_REGISTER.md D-46 by that row's own cheaper option: RunStatus gains ONE OPTIONAL PROPERTY, terminal_detail. A failed run could say a dependency was unavailable and could not say WHICH, because the domain catalog's safe_detail_keys live on the ErrorEnvelope and a 200 run reading is not an error envelope. It is the same shape and the same rule as ErrorEnvelope.details -- safe scalar classifiers, maxProperties 16, propertyNames ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$, scalar values bounded at 256 -- restricted to the keys the catalog declares for the code in terminal_reason, and present only beside one, because the allowlist that bounds it is a property of the reported code. NO component schema was added: the shape is declared inline exactly as ErrorEnvelope.details is, which is why component_schemas stays 51. NO error code was added: a distinct code for a replay miss was the row's option 2 and is a second reseal, which the owner did not take, so contracts/domain/v1/error-codes.json is untouched and stays at twenty-two. The sentence this makes sayable is 'your document is fine, the provider is fine, this deployment has no recording for it', which R-30 made the ordinary case by putting the alpha stand in recorded mode. Migration 0010_run_terminal_detail adds audit_run.terminal_detail, a separate revision from 0009 so that reverting this reseal does not also un-name every reviewer.

This reseal lands all four documents in ONE commit, because four documents moving together is the property D-18 exists to protect and a lock that trails its own contract by a commit is a window in which the frontend reads a digest the backend does not serve. A commit cannot name itself, so the field names 667a49c instead -- feat(R-37), the commit that made the corrected author_label description TRUE, and the nearest commit this document can honestly point at. THE AUTHORITY IS THE DIGEST, not this field: sha256 above is computed over the contract's own bytes and is what the drift guard compares.
openapi.read_only: A5 generates from contracts/api/v1/** and never edits it: a client and a contract reconciled by the same hand prove nothing. The seam is repaired only by the session that owns it - the FindingDetail repair was made by A7-FIX in contracts/api/v1/**, and this client regenerated from the result.

generator.determinism: Output is a pure function of the input bytes. No timestamp, hostname, absolute path or environment value is emitted; every iteration order is an explicit locale-independent sort, because localeCompare is locale-dependent. Two runs on the same document produce byte-identical files.

generated.hand_editing: forbidden; every file carries a do-not-edit header and the drift guard compares bytes

commands.makefile: none. OD-16 forbids adding a Makefile target for the frontend, so every command is `npm --prefix web run ...`.
